answer: Use clone divergence checkpoint. At dawn, the coordinator publishes a random seed; every identity must return a signed checkpoint (its anchor) extending only its prior checkpoint, so clones sharing state cannot satisfy two differing labels at once. A sparrow challenge then requires each identity to answer from a separate live execution slot; an attacker pays one dedicated process, storage namespace, and per-query compute (e.g., 0.5 CPU-second) for every identity it wants to keep concurrent. Failures freeze that identity until it buys a fresh slot and replays the full checkpoint chain.
